subject: MSA & Order Form — model-retrain consent and output rights
messages:
From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@quantifai.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Bhatt <asha@quantifai.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — training/use of customer data

Hi Ethan / Laura,

Attaching QuantifAI's tracked changes to the MSA and Order Form. Two high-priority asks from procurement and legal:

1) Customer must retain title to all Outputs generated by the service and have the right to use/redistribute them without restrictions.
2) Customer requires an explicit prohibition on using their data or outputs to train or improve provider models unless they opt in.

Both items are dealbreakers for our board unless there are very narrow carveouts. Please let me know if Redwood can agree to a plain-language clause along these lines: "Provider will not use Customer Content, including generated Outputs, to train, fine-tune, or improve Provider models without Customer's prior written consent. Provider may retain anonymized, aggregated telemetry for service operation and reliability reporting only."

We flagged this to legal and GC (Tom Reynolds) and they may follow up with more specific redlines; I'm looping Asha on procurement logistics.

Attachments: QuantifAI_MSA_tracked_changes.pdf

Next steps: need consolidated position from Redwood legal + product today so we can move to procurement approval.

Thanks,
Sarah Jones
Senior Procurement Manager | QuantifAI
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@quantifai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — training/use of customer data

Hi Sarah — thanks for the tracked changes and callout. (On Thu, Nov 12, 2026 at 9:12 AM Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@quantifai.com> wrote:)
> Attaching QuantifAI's tracked changes to the MSA and Order Form. Two high-priority asks ...

Quick response from our side: we understand the ask for output ownership — Redwood does not assert title over customer outputs for normal API usage. The training prohibition is where we typically push for a narrow, operationally necessary carveout.

Our proposed compromise (high level):
- Customer owns Outputs and may use/redistribute them.
- Redwood will not retrain or fine-tune models on raw Customer Content or generated Outputs without explicit, documented opt-in.
- Redwood reserves the right to use de-identified, aggregated telemetry and feedback signals to improve service quality (e.g., throughput, ranking, bug fixes), provided that such use cannot be reverse-engineered to recreate Customer Content.

Operational impacts to call out so procurement understands tradeoffs: disabling our ability to use customer prompts/outputs for modeling means we cannot provide certain Optimize features (automatic prompt caching, model-level contextual improvements) and may need to disable cross-customer telemetry that helps detect regressions. That can increase cost and slow incident detection.

Attached is a draft response we usually send back that sketches the language (proposed_redline_response.docx). I'll also escalate to legal/product to confirm precise wording and tech controls (KMS, deletion SLA, logging) — looping Neha and Laura for support.

Propose a 30-min legal/product sync tomorrow if that works for Tom and your team.

Best,
Ethan Park
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:00:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: QuantifAI MSA — suggested negotiation posture

Laura / Neha — internal thread capturing quick product + legal asks before we get GC note. I want to be prescriptive so procurement gets a single reply. Proposed posture:

1) Language proposal (short):
- Outputs: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in Outputs produced by the Service. Provider grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide license to use Outputs."
- Training: "Provider will not use Customer Content or Outputs to train or improve Provider's base or derivative models without Customer's prior written consent. Provider may continue to use de-identified, aggregated telemetry for service reliability and safety."

2) Tech controls we should offer (minimum):
- Opt-out/opt-in flag per workspace or API key that prevents any retention/use for modeling.
- 90-day raw request retention by default; customer can request immediate purge with documented SLA (we need legal to confirm acceptable language).
- KMS-backed encryption for customer data at rest and clear audit logs for access.

3) Commercial/ops tradeoffs to present:
- If QuantifAI opts out of telemetry/modeling, Redwood cannot provide automatic prompt-caching or cross-customer quality tuning; consider a small usage uplift or loss of certain Optimize features.
- Support/SLA impacts (longer MTTR for regressions).

Questions for legal/product:
- Can we commit to "no retrain without written consent" language? (Neha)
- Is 90-day retention acceptable as default or do we need to propose 30/60/90 options? (Laura)

I'll wait for Neha's legal read — if we get a green light we can send a consolidated reply to Sarah and Tom with attachments.

Ethan
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@quantifai.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@quantifai.com>, Asha Bhatt <asha@quantifai.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — training/use of customer data

Ethan — thanks for the quick reply and proposed compromise. A few notes from QuantifAI legal after an initial review:

1) We can accept "anonymized, aggregated telemetry" only if you confirm that (a) telemetry is irreversible (cannot be reconstructed into Customer Content), (b) you will provide sample telemetry schema, and (c) there is an auditable deletion process.
2) We need to see SOC2 or equivalent evidence for your logging/controls and a summary of KMS integration options.
3) We propose an explicit sentence that Provider will not perform model training on Customer Content or Outputs "for the purpose of improving models used to provide services to other customers" without written consent. (We can discuss carveouts for internal bug fixes.)

We attached a short PDF with legal comments (QuantifAI_legal_comments.pdf). We also prefer that any opt-in to allow training be explicit (separate form or DocuSign), not implied by acceptance of the standard TOS.

Happy to take the 30-min sync. Please propose times next week.

Tom Reynolds
General Counsel | QuantifAI
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@quantifai.com>, Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@quantifai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — training/use of customer data (proposal + next steps)

Tom / Sarah — appreciate the clear legal notes. Summarizing a negotiated position that aligns with product controls and minimizes operational surprises. If this looks good to you, we'll prepare the formal redline and DocuSign package.

Proposed confirmed language (draft for redline):
1) Outputs: "Customer owns all Outputs generated by the Service. Provider agrees not to assert ownership over Customer Outputs and grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, transferable license to use, reproduce, modify and distribute Outputs."
2) Training/Model Use: "Provider will not use Customer Content or Customer Outputs to train, fine-tune, or improve Provider's models that are used to serve other customers, unless Customer provides prior written consent via a separate opt-in agreement. Provider may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service reliability, product analytics, and security purposes, provided such data cannot be used to reconstruct Customer Content."
3) Controls and Evidence: Provider will offer an opt-in/opt-out setting at the workspace or API key level, KMS integration for customer-managed keys, and an audit log for data access. Provider will share SOC2 or equivalent evidence upon reasonable request.
4) Retention and Deletion: By default, Provider retains raw request data for 90 days to support debugging and incident response. Customer may request expedited purging subject to a documented SLA.

Operational impacts (for procurement): if QuantifAI elects to opt out of sharing data for modeling, certain Redwood Optimize features (automatic cross-customer tuning, shared prompt caching) will be disabled for the account and may result in higher unit cost or slightly higher latency on particular flows. We will document the feature differences in the order form appendix.

Next steps:
- If QuantifAI agrees to the above, Redwood will send a single redline and addendum for the Order Form.
- Schedule 30-min call next Tue/Wed — suggest Tue 11/17 at 10:00 PT; I can send a calendar invite.
- Finalize DocuSign package after legal redline.

Attachments: proposed_redline_response.docx

Let me know if any of this is a non-starter. If Tom wants stronger deletion language or a shorter retention window we can escalate product feasibility.

Thanks,
Ethan Park
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
